To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have not detected any [O ii], and that the SFR upper limits derived from this non detection are lower than previous SFR values derived from IR and SED luminosity, implying that the extinction in the SMGs is higher.
the SFR derived from the [O II] emission lines is at least two orders lower than that obtained from the SED and infrared luminosities, which suggests high internal extinction.
the SINFONI data do not detect any [O ii], and that the upper limit to the SFR of the SMGs are at least two order of magnitudes lower than the SED-based estimates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search of the unobscurred star formation in SMGs and LAEs at z ∼ 5.
the search for the [O ii] emission lines in the K -band spectra of two SMG systems, which have previously been studied in the optical and infrared bands.
a detailed analysis of the [O II] doublet emission line in SMGs, in particular, with the search for this line in the K -band spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data do not show any evidence for unobscured (or partially obscured) star formation activity in these two SMG systems, but the upper limit to the SFR derived from [O ii], and the internal extinction derived from this upper limit, are consistent with those obtained from SED fitting, IR luminosities and the [O iii]/[O ii] line ratios.
, at least for the objects of these two systems, the [O II] λλ 3706, 3729 A emission line is not the best tracer of the unobscurred SFR in SMGs and LAEs.
the unobscurred star formation in these systems is not detected, and that the internal extinction in SMGs is at least two orders-of-magnitude larger than in the LAEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SED-derived SFRs for the submillimeter galaxies are likely to be dominated by dust-enshrouded star formation, whereas the SEDs for the LAEs are consistent with being dominated by unobscured, or moderately obscured star formation.

, for the SMGs, the [O  ii]-based SFRs are at least one order lower than those derived by the SED and IR tracers, and the extinction is high enough that the [O II] line is completely obscured in the K band.
the [O II] doublet emission line is not a good tracer of the unobscurred SFR in SMGs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [O i] λ 6300 and [O ii], λλ 3727, 29 doublet are not detected in any of our targets.
the [O II] doublet is an excellent tracer of the unobscurred SFR in SMGs and LAEs at high redshift.
the [O II]-based SFR is lower than the one derived from the IR and the SED-fitting methods.
